name: When should I repair versus completely replace my bathroom tile?

mainEntity.name: When should I repair versus completely replace my bathroom tile?

acceptedAnswer.text: You should replace your bathroom tile if you notice hollow-sounding tiles, persistent cracked or loose pieces, crumbly grout that refuses to hold, or persistent mildew behind caulked seams. These symptoms often signal that water has bypassed the tile layer and compromised the substrate beneath. Soft spots in the floor near the tub or toilet are critical signs that the subfloor is rotting and needs immediate attention. HH Remodeling can evaluate whether localized repairs will suffice or if a full tear-out and subfloor restoration is necessary.
acceptedAnswer.description: Replace tile if you observe widespread loose tiles, crumbling grout, spongy floors, or water stains, which indicate moisture has reached the subfloor or wall studs.
